Amazon .com sells books, music and other items over the Internet and is one of the pioneers of consumer e-business. Amazon, based in Seattle, started by filling all orders using books purchased form a distributor in response to customer orders. The practice differs from that of traditional book store which usually purchases directly from publishers and stock books in anticipation of customer order. Today, Amazon has six warehouses where it holds inventory. Amazon stocks best-selling books, through it still gets other titles from distributors or publishers, It uses the U.S. Postal Services and other package carriers such as UPS and FedEx to send books to customers. Amazon continued to expand the set of products that it sells online. Besides books and music, Amazon has added many products categories such as toys appeal, electronics, jewelry and shoes. Qu.4 — Gateway is a manufacturer of PCs that was founded in 1985 and started as a direct sales manufacturer with no retail footprint. In 1996, Gateway was one of the first PC manufacturer to start selling PCs online. Over the years Gateway expanded its operation worldwide, with sales and manufacturing presence in Europe and Asia Pacific. In 1999, the company had three plants in the United States, a plant in Ireland and one more in Malaysia. In late 1009s, Géteway introduced an aggressive strategy of opening Gateway retail stores throughout United States. By J; anuary 2002, Gateway had approximately 280 retail stores in the United States. Gateway strategy was to avoid carrying any finished goods inventory at the retail stores and simply use these stores for customers to try the PCs and obtain help in deciding on the right configuration to purchase. When customers placed their orders, PCs were manufactured to order and shipped from one of the assembly plants. Initially, investors rewarded Gateway for this strategy and raised the stock price to more than $80 per sharé in late 1999. However, this success did not last. By November 2002, Gateway shares had dropped to less than $4 and Gateway was losing a significant amount of money. Plants in Salt Lake City Ireland and Malaysia were shut. By April 2004, Gateway had closed all its retail outlets and reduced the number of confi gurations offered to customers. The company was looking to sell its PCs through electronic retailers such as Best Buy and Circuit City. As you can imagine, this was quite a transition for the company to experience. af Qu.5 Answer the following questions highlight supply chain decisions that have a bearing on Gateway’s performance: a) How does Gateway decide which production facility will produce and ship a customer order? b) What factors did Gateway consider when deciding which plants to close?
